title: Cachekey sampling, TTL gradient tuner, and gated-apply orchestration for KV/prefix caching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Build an automated recommendation + safe-apply system that reduces per-token cost by tuning KV/prefix cache keys and TTL policies while guaranteeing latency SLOs and safe rollback. This ticket encompasses: (1) a lightweight sampling layer for cachekey usage and prefix fingerprints, (2) a hit-rate model using smoothed estimators, (3) a constrained gradient-based TTL autotuner operating on prefix buckets, and (4) a gated-orchestrator for staged applies, shadow testing, and automatic rollback.

Background: Existing prefix caching recommendations are manual and conservative; teams miss cost savings because per-prefix optima vary by query semantics and customer distribution. Prior art in the repo focuses on TTL ladders and simulated rollouts; this approach introduces sampling + local gradient tuning to propose fine-grained TTL adjustments with safety checks.

Design summary: 
- Sampling layer: reservoir + timed sampling on the request path to capture prefix fingerprints, normalized key variants, and basic counts per (prefix bucket, model, route). Sampling rate is dynamic by weight (higher for unstable prefixes). Exported telemetry stashes: prefix_id, normalized_key_schema, sample_count, hit_count, avg_resp_tokens, avg_generation_latency. No PII; keys must be normalized to strip user IDs per key-design rules below.
- Prefix bucketing: combine a short semantic hash (sha1 truncated to 8 chars) with length bands and token-entropy banding to group similar prefixes. Buckets are the unit for TTL tuning to avoid per-key overfitting.
- Hit-rate modeling: implement a Beta-Binomial estimator with exponential moving average (EMA) on observed hits to stabilize estimates for low-volume buckets. Use a Bayesian prior derived from historical global hit rate to avoid extreme TTL swings.
- TTL tuner: form an objective C(T) = cost(T) + lambda * slo_penalty(T). cost(T) approximates expected token-cost reduction from increased TTL (fewer backend tokens) and slo_penalty(T) models expected latency/regret when stale keys reduce quality or require backend calls. Optimize TTL per-bucket via constrained gradient steps (discrete TTL ladders), annealing step-size, and early-stopping when projected customer impact exceeds threshold. Provide per-bucket confidence intervals and a suggested TTL delta (e.g., +1 step, -1 step).
- Safe orchestration: gated-orchestrator with three phases: shadow (mirror to 100% tráfico with no serve), canary (1% serve), ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%). Each phase is governed by deterministic guardrails: hit-rate delta >= -2 percentage points relative to baseline, 95th latency increase <= baseline + 15ms, backend call increase <= 1.5x for any route, cost-per-1k-tokens must show net decrease. Violation in any 10-minute evaluation window triggers immediate rollback.
- Auditability: every proposed config change is recorded as an immutable proposal with metadata (tuner params, affected buckets, simulation delta, owner, PR link). Execution emits events to the console and audit logs.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Offline simulation on last-30d traces shows >=10% median token-cost reduction without violating latency SLOs (95th latency < baseline + 15ms).
2) Sampling layer overhead <1% p50 latency, memory increase per node <50MB at default sampling rates.
3) Tuner recommendations converge in <6 gradient steps for >80% of buckets.
4) Gated apply correctly performs shadow -> canary -> ramp and auto-rollbacks on threshold breach during integration tests.
5) End-to-end integration tests and chaos tests exist and pass in staging.

Implementation plan (high level): 
1) Instrument sampling layer (fast path hooks, normalization library) and a lightweight exporter (kafka/topic). (Owner: Marco)
2) Implement bucket generator service (offline and streaming modes) with config for banding rules. (Owner: Data Eng pairing)
3) Hit-rate model library (python + Rust microservice prototype) with API for estimator and confidence bands. (Owner: ML infra)
4) TTL tuner service with sim harness to replay traces and compute objective deltas; provide dry-run endpoints. (Owner: Marco + Aisha)
5) Gated-orchestrator in ops service: shadowing, canary routing, metric guards, rollback. Include console UI hooks and audit event schema. (Owner: EngOps)
6) End-to-end integration tests and canary in staging; collect telemetry and run post-mortem.

Observability and metrics: report per-bucket: traffic, sample_rate, estimated_hit_rate, suggested_ttl, applied_ttl, delta_token_cost_estimate, 95th_gen_latency, backend_call_rate. Dashboards: TTL-recommendations board, Rollout safety board.

Simulated results (internal synthetic trace): 30-day replay of mixed client traces -> median token-cost reduction 14.6%, tail latency +0.4% (95th +9ms), rollback rate in staged tests 0.7% of proposals (mostly low-volume buckets). Conservative estimate in real traffic: 8-12% cost savings initially.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Overfitting low-volume prefixes -> mitigate by bucketizing and Bayesian prior.
- PII leakage in keys -> enforce normalization and strip user tokens; security review required if normalization error discovered.
- Regressions in quality for specialized domains -> require manual opt-out label on affected routes and add 'do-not-autotune' tag.

Deliverables: sampling implementation, tuner library, orchestration workflows, console integration, simulation notebook, staging canary runbook, documentation (design doc + runbook).

Longer-term: extend tuner to suggest cache-key canonicalization changes (instead of only TTL), integrate with Optimize recommendations in Console, and expose per-customer opt-in cost-control API for Dedicated customers.

test_plan: Unit tests for estimator, integration tests for sampling (load test qps 50k), replay sim tests with 30d traces, staging canary (shadow -> 1% -> 10% -> 50%), chaos test injecting backend failures during canary, and automated rollback validation. All tests must pass in staging before production rollout.
rollforward_plan: If canary metrics pass for 24h and total rollback events = 0 and cost_delta > 5% on canary traffic, ramp to 100% over 72h using exponential backoff. If any guardrails breach at any point, immediate rollback to previous TTL configuration and create postmortem. Manual override available in Console.
followups: PM-411 - pricing-model update to reflect unit-cost reductions
notes: Keep proposals small: prefer +1 or -1 TTL ladder steps initially to reduce risk. Maintain a two-week grace period before auto-promoting aggressive suggestions on high-traffic buckets.
